## Static statistic description 
o\*net is dataset about the occupations and their characteristics in the U.S. Based on my project about the relationship between occupations and skills required by occupations, I chose this dataset including the major types of occupations (industry, preparation level), occupation codes and titles, 35 occupation skills, education level required by the occupations, and the skill dimension I extarcted before. Specifically, for each skill, we have a score for their importance in this occupation from 0-5 (continuous variables), and other variables are categorical variables. I chose 3 skills in each factor dimension, so we have 12 skills in total. 
Specifically, we have:
  1. occupation unique codes and titles 
  2. job zone (the preparation level needed before people enter these occupations)
  3. major groups (the major type of occupations)
  4. scores on skill dimensions
  5. scores on 12 specific skills
  

```{r}
#read data
library(tidyverse)
data <- read.csv("onet_2026_clean.csv") |>
  mutate (preparation = factor(job_zone, levels = c("Little","Medium","Considerable","Extensive" )))

```


```{r}
# investigate data
table(data$job_zone)
table(data$major_group)
table(data$skill_type)

table(data$preparation, data$major_group)
table(data$major_group, data$skill_type)
table(data$preparation, data$skill_type)

```
```{r}
# investigate data - summarize the continous variables
# write a function to make good programming 
summarise_onet <- function(x){
  data |> 
    group_by(.data[[x]]) |>
    summarise(across(where(is.numeric), list(mean = mean, median = median, sd = sd)))
}
summarise_onet("preparation")
summarise_onet("skill_type")
summarise_onet("major_group")
```
